paper.title: Fabrication and Welding of High-Yield Strength Steels for Submarine Hulls (HY-80 Specification)
paper.author: Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA)
paper.institution: United States Department of the Navy

steel.name: HY-80
steel.alloy_family: quenched and tempered high-yield martensitic naval steel

evidence.claim: Carbon content balanced between strength and weldability
Imparts solid solution toughness and lowers ductile-to-brittle transition temperature
Prevents temper embrittlement during slow cooling

processing.notes: Full austenitization to form lath martensite upon quenching.
High temperature tempering to precipitate carbides and restore impact toughness.

evidence.claim: Homogeneous tempered martensite with fine carbide dispersion
Minimum 80 ksi (552 MPa) yield strength specification
Minimum 50 ft-lb Charpy V-notch energy at -84C (-120F)

weldability_indicators.notes: Requires strict preheat (93-150C) and interpass control to avoid hydrogen-induced heat affected zone cracking.

evidence.claim: Nickel lowers the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature without reducing strength
Molybdenum prevents impurity segregation to grain boundaries during tempering

design_rationale: Quenched and tempered martensite achieves a baseline 80 ksi yield strength for submarine pressure hulls.
2.75 wt% Ni ensures sub-zero Charpy toughness down to -84C.
Higher carbon (0.15 wt%) necessitates strict welding preheat controls.
